subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw treat enrolled-speaker matching as a supported voice command gate, and if so where should enrollment, profile storage, matching thresholds, fallback behavior, and provider egress policy live?
rationale: The request is useful but cannot be safely reduced to a narrow fix because it adds biometric-like state, probabilistic authorization behavior, and cross-platform voice runtime ownership choices.

options.title: Design speaker gating first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the security/product contract and the owner boundary for native, realtime, and plugin implementations.

options.title: Prototype outside core
options.body: Ask for a ClawHub/plugin or local prototype only if current extension hooks can prove the path without adding core biometric state or command-gating policy.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave current wake-word, push-to-talk, and Talk behavior unchanged until there is stronger maintainer demand or a lower-risk platform API path.

recommendation.title: Design speaker gating first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the security/product contract and the owner boundary for native, realtime, and plugin implementations.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is broad ownership of the macOS Voice Wake, push-to-talk, Talk, and config architecture this decision would coordinate.
